subject: phoenix
pitch: A phoenix rising with its wings flung open. Feathers blaze from deep crimson at the body through orange to golden yellow at the tips, a crest of flame-shaped plumes on its head, long trailing tail feathers like ribbons of fire, glowing amber eyes and a golden hooked beak. Embers and sparks drift off its wings.
reasoning:
I only have partial access to the SDK reference, so I need to stick to the well-documented API calls I'm confident about — things like creating joints, chains, sweeps, parts, spikes, and extrusions — rather than risk guessing at unknown signatures.

Since orientation parameters for b.part are uncertain, I'll play it safe by building geometries in model space and baking transforms directly into them rather than relying on unclear "aim"/"dir"/"up" options. For attaching parts to the skeleton, I'll pass the bone explicitly as a joint reference since that's the one option I'm confident is supported.

I'm sketching the overall pose now: a phoenix in flight facing +Z, body tilted upward around y~1.6, legs dangling down to about y~0.9 with talons, and a trailing tail that reaches down to touch y=0 so the lowest point rests on the ground plane. For the feathers, I'll write a helper that builds a thin extruded leaf-shaped geometry oriented along an arbitrary direction vector using a basis matrix, with colors blended via linear interpolation to create gradient feather tips.

Now I'm planning the wing structure: mirrored joints (shoulder, elbow, wrist, tip) on each side, with rows of feathers fanning outward — short crimson coverts, medium orange secondaries, and long golden primaries — and each individual feather split into two or three colored segments to fake a gradient from base to tip since I'm limited to a small flat color palette.

Writing feather geometry function...

For hanging tail feathers the normal points toward z. I'm working out the wing feather fan directions, sweeping primaries outward and backward from the wrist with angles from -20° to 80°, and roughing out overall proportions—wingspan around 7-8m, wrist at x=2.2, wing tips rising to about 3.5, body centered near y=2.4 with the tail trailing down to the ground.

For the tail I'm building ribbon geometry by sampling points along a bezier curve and offsetting by the binormal to get width, constructing it as double-sided colored quad strips in segments rather than using tube geometry, since the material needs flat shading and quantized vertex colors along the curve.

Totaling it up: wings around 210 feather parts, tail 56, crest a few dozen, keeping the whole bird under 1000 low-triangle segments. I'm defining a color ramp from deep crimson at the body to bright golden-yellow at the tips, with a colorAt function blending each feather's position along the wing with its own tip gradient.

Now I'm quantizing those gradient values to a limited set of steps to keep the material palette small, then building the body as a tilted, elongated ellipsoid representing a rising bird pose with a helper function to place each part with its own geometry, color, and transform matrix.

I'm working through whether omitting the "at" parameter defaults to origin placement, assuming the bone attachment system handles local-space transforms automatically, then sketching out the skeleton hierarchy—body, chest, neck segments, head, and jaw joints with their approximate positions.

Still mapping skeleton positions...

Still working out feather geometry...

Now I'm planning embers as small glowing-colored spheres scattered on the bone root and wings, plus the head details: a sphere skull with a hooked beak cone, lower jaw cone, amber eyes with dark pupils, seven flame-shaped crest ribbons rising back from the head, gold cylinder legs with cone talons, and a ring of roughly fourteen small chest feathers layered like scales, keeping everything quick and simple.

I'm defining width-curve functions for the flame plumes and leaf-shaped feathers using tapered sine-based falloffs, then working out the ribbon-building logic: given a path of points, a width function, and a hint vector, I compute a tangent and perpendicular side vector at each station to place left/right edge vertices, then stitch adjacent stations into quad segments.

Writing geometry triangles...

Writing ribbon and feather geometry functions...

Defining feather heat gradients and arm path interpolation for the wing, then laying out the covert row positions and angles along the shoulder-to-wingtip path.

Still tuning feather geometry...

For the tail, I'm laying out seven ribbons using cubic bezier curves, spreading their side offsets symmetrically and making the middle ribbons extend longer and lower toward the floor than the outer ones, with a slight S-curve variation planned for the control points.

I'm computing the ribbon widths and tail colors for the flame effect, then setting up the bezier curves for the tail and the seven crest plumes fanning out from the head.

Working out breast feather placement on the pitched ellipsoid body, computing ring positions and angles for a grid of rows around the chest for a natural ruffled look.

Tallying up totals, the part count is getting large so I'm trimming the breast section to fewer rows to keep things manageable. Now I'm working out the neck geometry, stacking tapered cylinder segments from the chest up to the head sphere, adjusting positions to account for the body's tilt angle.

Next I'm shaping the beak with cones for the upper and lower jaw pointing forward, adding a small curved hook at the tip, and picking gold tones for the beak color. Then I'm placing small amber eye spheres with dark pupils near the head front.

Now I'm building the legs with thigh, shin, and foot segments down to toed feet with forward and back claws, all in gold tones, then scattering embers as small octahedrons with varied sizes and colors around and beneath the wings for a fiery particle effect.

I'm also setting up a heat-based color ramp function and a helper for constructing tapered rod geometry between two points, which I'll use to build limb segments consistently.
